references.title: GR00T 2: Scaling Robot Foundation Models for Generalization, Dexterity, and Adaptation
references.summary: GR00T 2 is a world-action model that jointly predicts future video and robot actions. Its official material separates three improvement mechanisms: policy post-training and real-world RL, an execution agent invoking the WAM API, and ASPIRE-authored code recovery skills. The agent watches for stalls, calls a code skill to repair the scene, then hands control back. Turbo compresses the video representation and model for onboard execution, with SONIC providing faster whole-body control.
references.verification: Primary project methods and evaluation text read on 2026-11-22; performance claims remain author-reported.
references.source_origin: Public search result and existing atlas link

The page also reports limits of visual steering: marks do not encode final object orientation or all motion, and some long tasks still rarely complete.

references.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5: Accelerating Physical Intelligence
references.summary: Gemini Robotics 2.5 is the robot action model; Gemini Robotics ER tracks workflow in the described automotive-kitting pilot. Gemini 4 Argon acts elsewhere in the development loop, building simulation practice data and helping diagnose rollout failures. These roles make this a useful concrete example of combining action execution, high-level supervision and agent-assisted learning.
references.verification: Primary project methods and evaluation text read on 2026-11-22; performance claims remain author-reported.
references.limitations: The company post reports task breadth, dexterity and a factory proof-of-concept; it does not supply independent verification or demonstrate unconstrained generalist deployment. The factory result is a particular kitting workflow, not a measured rate across all robot work.

references.title: GRAIL: Generating Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from World Models
references.summary: GRAIL grounds video generation in known 3D assets before reconstruction: geometry, cameras, metric scale and a robot-proportioned character are fixed inputs. Recovered human-object interaction is retargeted to a humanoid, then object-aware and scene-aware trackers convert it into robot-action data for downstream visual policy learning. This is a generated-training-data pipeline, rather than the robot performing online search in a video model.
references.verification: Primary project methods and evaluation text read on 2026-11-22; performance claims remain author-reported.
references.source_origin: Public search result and existing atlas link
references.limitations: Privileged scene information simplifies reconstruction and avoids the assumptions of unconstrained in-the-wild video recovery. Physical transfer examples are particular pickup and stair tasks; broad generation capability is not automatically broad deployed autonomy.

references.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
references.summary: RoboTTT integrates test-time-training layers into a robot policy. Their fast weights are fixed-size recurrent state: incoming tokens update those weights, and the updated state conditions actions. Sequence action forcing and truncated backpropagation enable long-sequence training. DAgger Distillation uses mistakes as context and corrections as action targets, giving a mechanism for within-episode recovery.
references.verification: Primary project methods and evaluation text read on 2026-11-22; performance claims remain author-reported.
references.limitations: Fast weights and persistent trained parameters play different roles. The reviewed assembly evaluations demonstrate context-dependent behavior; they do not establish that slow policy weights continually update across real deployments.

references.title: SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model
references.summary: SuperMimic learns one differentiable world model of shared humanoid dynamics and jointly trains a tracking policy through imagined short rollouts. Gradients pass through the learned model rather than the rigid-body simulator. Its main contribution is amortizing this learning across a motion library, giving a practical alternative to repeatedly training specialists or using cluster-scale model-free RL.
references.verification: Indexed paper abstract and primary project method/evaluation text read; full indexed paper methods were unavailable on 2026-11-22; performance claims remain author-reported.
references.limitations: The official project page states that benchmark motions are training motions for both methods, so failure counts measure coverage, not generalization. Comparisons also use different GPU hardware and motion-data amounts; the report distinguishes return, wall time and GPU-hours.

references.title: DreamZero: World Action Models are Zero-shot Policies
references.summary: DreamZero learns a policy from a pretrained video-diffusion backbone by jointly predicting video and actions. Its official page separates novel task/environment tests, task-specific post-training, and new-embodiment adaptation with play data. Runtime optimization, asynchronous inference and smoothing are part of deploying the model, alongside the learning recipe.
references.limitations: “Zero-shot” is conditioned on the test axis. New embodiment adaptation uses target-robot play data, then tests novel tasks or objects; it is not strict no-target-exposure transfer. The reviewed page describes its own real-robot comparisons, and a visual rollout gallery does not replace a matched benchmark protocol.
references.verification: Primary project method and evaluation text read on 2026-11-22; empirical findings remain author-reported.

references.title: Gemini 4 Argon for Robotics
references.summary: The Argon primary post gives distinct examples of robot-control primitives, physically calibrated Real2Sim, hindsight annotation, simulation-generated training experience and iterative hardware repair. Its simulation reconstruction example separately checks visual match and force/torque timing, magnitude and direction. This makes the agent-run learning branch concrete: an agent can create experiments and accepted code/data artifacts without every example implying neural-weight learning.
references.limitations: The examples are company demonstrations with supplied prompts, hardware primitives and verification objectives. The iterative pick-and-place example improves an execution artifact; the simulation-data example supports a VLA training loop. Neither demonstrates recursive self-improvement of the underlying model or unlimited autonomy.
references.verification: Primary article sections on control, calibration and research loops read on 2026-11-22; empirical findings remain author-reported.

references.title: π0.7: A Steerable Generalist Robotic Foundation Model with Emergent Capabilities
references.summary: π0.7 diversifies the conditioning context, including subtask instructions, subgoal images, control modes and episode metadata. This lets a single model learn from demonstrations, suboptimal autonomous trajectories including failures, and non-robot sources while giving users more ways to specify desired behavior. The paper evaluates instruction following, cross-embodiment transfer and compositional tasks.
references.limitations: The authors explicitly say large, diverse data makes definitive seen-versus-unseen task classification difficult: related skills can appear under other labels or incidentally. Treat its out-of-the-box demonstrations as evidence under its data assumptions, and compare strict embodiment holdout separately.
references.verification: Indexed paper method, evaluation and discussion sections read on 2026-11-22; empirical findings remain author-reported.

references.title: FlowEval: How Much Adaptation Does an Embodied Foundation Model Need at Deployment?
references.summary: FlowEval uses a small set of successful target-domain demonstrations and the flow-matching objective to diagnose model–deployment fit without training. It probes predictive agreement and studies whether the score correlates with improvement as adaptation data is added. It supplies a useful decision layer before collecting another large dataset: diagnose what adaptation may remain, then test that prediction.
references.limitations: The method applies to flow-matching action models. It assumes actual rollout demonstrations with the issued action targets; post-hoc reconstructed action targets can invalidate the metric. The paper identifies calibrated predictions of the exact amount of data needed as future work, so correlation is not a guaranteed data-budget estimate.
references.verification: Indexed paper method, adaptation experiments and stated limitations read on 2026-11-22; empirical findings remain author-reported.

references.title: VLRLA: Deployment-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language-Action Models through In-Context Reinforcement Learning
references.summary: VLRLA conditions actions on accumulated observations, actions, rewards and termination signals while keeping deployed model parameters fixed. Its in-context RL module learns during training how to use interaction history; deployment then changes the history rather than optimizing the checkpoint. The paper includes simulation studies and real tasks with cross-episode reward memory.
references.limitations: Fixed weights do not mean fixed behavior, but this is still distinct from persistent weight adaptation. Its histories and reward feedback are designed inputs, and the reported transfer is bounded by the evaluated tasks and training-history construction strategies.
references.verification: Indexed paper design, simulation and real-experiment sections read on 2026-11-22; empirical findings remain author-reported.

references.title: Dual-Stream Memory for Vision-Language-Action Policies
references.summary: Dual-Stream Memory separates compressed execution-stage context from selective access to historical visual detail. A task-agnostic Gated DeltaNet produces a compact temporal token; a task-conditioned retriever keeps relevant frames with spatial detail. This refines the memory question from “how long a context?” to “which information should be compressed, and which must remain accessible?”.
references.limitations: The paper reports non-additive benefits and task regressions, and real gains concentrate on repeated actions. Real checkpoints are matched by training loss rather than equal training steps. The authors call for matched full-system ablations and broader task/hardware tests, especially identity tracking through cup swaps.
references.verification: Indexed paper method, full-benchmark comparison and real-robot evaluation read on 2026-11-22; empirical findings remain author-reported.

references.title: ODE Policy: Robot Learning via Action Dynamics, Not Actions
references.summary: ODE Policy learns a vector field for how robot commands evolve in physical time, then integrates it to produce an action trajectory. This is different from the denoising time of a generative flow head. The paper studies seamless chunk joins, small perturbations near demonstrations and a diversity head, with comparisons in imitation learning, VLA/WAM action heads and humanoid reinforcement learning.
references.limitations: The reported protocols use specific chunk lengths, integrators and control rates. Some execution-quality measures compare only successful episodes, while one real-task baseline measure comes from failures. The paper’s uses for arbitrary control rates and action-free learning include preliminary directions rather than finished solutions.
